candidates.title: [Bug]: nested member-access lvexpr evaluates the outer key after the inner key (wrong evaluation order)
candidates.body:
### Description
In a nested member-access lvexpr such as `a[i()][j()] = v`, the interpreter evaluates the inner lvexpr's key (`i()`) before the outer key (`j()`). Spec §7.15.1 prescribes the opposite order for `member-access-lvexpr := lvexpr [ expression ]`:

> It is evaluated as follows: evaluate expression to get a string or int k; evaluate lvexpr to get lvalue lv; perform a filling-read operation on lv to get a list or mapping value v; the result is an lvalue referring to the member of c with key k.

For the outermost node, `expression` is `f("inner", 0)` and `lvexpr` is `a[f("outer", 1)]`. So `inner` must be evaluated before `outer`. The RHS comes first under §7.15.2 ("execute action-or-expr to get a value v; evaluate lvexpr to get an lvalue lv; ..."), and the interpreter already gets that part right.

The difference only shows up with nested lvexprs. In a single-level `v[k()] = ...` the container is a plain variable, so the order can't be observed.

### Steps to Reproduce
```ballerina
import ballerina/io;

function f(string s, int v) returns int {
    io:println(s);
    return v;
}

public function main() {
    int[][] a = [[1, 2], [3, 4]];
    a[f("outer", 1)][f("inner", 0)] = f("rhs", 9);
    // @output rhs
    // @output inner
    // @output outer
    io:println(a); // @output [[1,2],[9,4]]
}
```
Run `go run ./cli/cmd run nested-lvexpr-order-v.bal`.

Actual output:
```
rhs
outer
inner
[[1,2],[9,4]]
```
Expected output:
```
rhs
inner
outer
[[1,2],[9,4]]
```

### Affected Version(s)
`main` @ be382dae

### OS, DB, other environment details and versions
Linux, Go toolchain from go.mod

### Related area
Interpreter

### Related issue(s) (optional)
- #1634: rvalue member access evaluates the key before the container. That issue notes that the lvexpr order is key-first per §7.15.1, but nested lvexprs currently evaluate container-first.
- #1217: compound assignment evaluates the lvexpr before the RHS.

### Suggested label(s) (optional)
Area/Interpreter

candidates.title: [Bug]: chained relational operators (`a < b < c`) are accepted although relational operators are non-associative
candidates.body:
### Description
Relational operators (`<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`) are non-associative according to the spec's expression precedence table, but the parser treats them as left-associative. A chained comparison such as `a < b < b` compiles, is parsed as `(a < b) < b`, and runs.

Spec, §6 (Expressions), precedence table ("The following table shows the various types of expression in decreasing order of precedence, together with associativity"):
- `x < y`, `x > y`, `x <= y`, `x >= y`, `x is y`, `x !is y`: associativity **non**
- `x == y`, `x != y`, `x === y`, `x !== y`: associativity **left**

With non-associativity, `a < b < b` has no valid parse, so it should be rejected at compile time. Only the equality operators are declared left-associative.

### Steps to Reproduce
```ballerina
import ballerina/io;

public function main() {
    boolean a = false;
    boolean b = true;
    io:println(a < b < b); // @error
}
```
Run `go run ./cli/cmd run relational-nonassoc-e.bal`.

Actual: compiles and prints `false`, which is the result of `(a < b) < b`.

Expected: a compile-time (syntax) error at the chained comparison.

Note: the spec doesn't spell out in prose what "non" associativity means. The usual reading is that the operator cannot be chained without parentheses. jBallerina was not checked here; the parser is derived from jBallerina's, so it may accept this too.

### Affected Version(s)
`main` @ be382dae

### OS, DB, other environment details and versions
Linux, Go toolchain from go.mod

### Related area
Parser

### Suggested label(s) (optional)
Area/Parser
